_about: Generic Manufacturing Estate Map (mock food & beverage manufacturer FBCo). Source: Oracle Fusion Cloud 26C guides; see manufacturing/00-overview.md. Built by tools/build_map_data.py --map manufacturing.

header.eyebrow: Generic reference · Oracle Fusion Cloud 26C · no client data
header.title: Manufacturing Estate Map
header.lede: A food and beverage manufacturer with a US parent and a Mexican subsidiary on Oracle Fusion ERP and SCM. Master data sits apart from transactions; each module shows its key processes, its open interfaces and the journal entries it creates. Select any module to see how it connects.

facts.label: ledger views (2 primary, 1 secondary, 1 reporting currency)

footer: Generic reference map built from the Oracle Fusion Cloud 26C implementation and user guides. FBCo is a mock company; items the guides don't cover are marked INFERRED in the knowledge pack.

nodes.title: Enterprise structure
nodes.subtitle: Legal entities · BUs · orgs
nodes.description: Two legal entities (FBCo US, FBCo México), a business unit each, inventory organisations for the plants and the distribution centre, and the cost organisations that value them.
functions: Legal entities own the ledgers and the tax registrations
Business units run Payables, Receivables and Procurement; profit-centre BUs own inventory
Inventory organisations: US plant, US distribution centre, MX plant
Cost organisations and cost books value each inventory organisation

nodes.title: Chart of accounts & ledgers
nodes.subtitle: Corporate COA · calendars · rates
nodes.description: One corporate chart of accounts for both countries, a chart of accounts mapping to the Mexican statutory chart, accounting calendars and daily rates.
functions: Corporate chart: Company, Cost centre, Account, Product line, Intercompany, Future
Account hierarchies (trees) for reporting and allocations
Cross-validation rules stop invalid account combinations
Chart of accounts mapping: corporate → Mexican statutory chart (SAT grouping code)
processes: Import Chart of Accounts Mapping Rules

nodes.title: Suppliers
nodes.subtitle: Ingredients · packaging · MRO
nodes.description: The supplier master: suppliers, sites, contacts, bank accounts and site assignments to the business units that buy and pay.
functions: Supplier registration and approval
Sites assigned to the procurement and invoicing business units
Bank accounts and payment methods for Payments
Tax registrations used by Tax on invoices
processes: Import Suppliers (sites, addresses, contacts, site assignments)

nodes.title: Customers
nodes.subtitle: Retail · food service
nodes.description: Customer accounts and sites for retail chains, distributors and food-service operators, with credit profiles and payment methods.
functions: Customer accounts, bill-to and ship-to sites
Customer profiles: payment terms, credit limits, dunning
Customer bank accounts and payment methods for automatic receipts

nodes.title: Items, recipes & costs
nodes.subtitle: Product Hub · work definitions
nodes.description: Items for ingredients, packaging and finished goods; work definitions (recipes) for process manufacturing; standard costs in the cost book.
functions: Items with lot control and shelf life (expiry dates)
Work definitions: ingredients in, primary output and co-products out
Dual units of measure where needed (litres and kilograms)
Standard costs loaded into the cost book

nodes.title: Banks & tax
nodes.subtitle: Bank accounts · US sales tax · MX VAT
nodes.description: Internal bank accounts for each legal entity, and the tax regimes Tax applies to purchases and sales: US sales and use tax, and Mexican VAT (IVA).
functions: Bank accounts used by Payments, Receivables and Cash Management
Tax regimes, rates and rules for both countries
Recoverable and payable tax accounts per regime

nodes.title: Customer orders
nodes.subtitle: EDI · customer portal
nodes.description: Retail purchase orders arrive by EDI; smaller customers order through a portal.
functions: Sends purchase orders to Order Management
Receives order acknowledgements, ship notices and invoices

nodes.title: Planning Central
nodes.subtitle: Demand & supply plan
nodes.description: Plans demand from forecasts and sales orders against on-hand and open supply, and recommends what to make and what to buy.
functions: Forecasts demand and nets it against on-hand and open supply
Creates planned orders for make and buy
Releases planned make orders as work orders and planned buy orders as requisitions

nodes.title: Self Service Procurement
nodes.subtitle: Requisitions
nodes.description: Employees and planners request goods and services; approved requisition lines become purchase orders.
functions: Catalogue and non-catalogue requests
Approval by amount and category
Approved lines → PO lines (automatic or by a buyer)

nodes.title: Purchasing
nodes.subtitle: Purchase orders · agreements
nodes.description: Purchase orders and agreements with ingredient and packaging suppliers; PO schedules become expected receipts.
functions: Blanket and contract agreements with price breaks
POs from requisitions or planning
Accrue-at-receipt for inventory lines; period-end accrual for expense lines

nodes.title: Supply Chain Orchestration
nodes.subtitle: Supply requests
nodes.description: Takes supply requests from planning and Order Management, creates the work order, transfer order or purchase order, and tracks it.
functions: Creates work orders from make requests
Creates transfer orders and purchase orders from buy and transfer requests
Raises exceptions when supply changes (for example a work order on hold)

nodes.title: Receiving
nodes.subtitle: Receive · inspect · put away
nodes.description: Receives goods against PO schedules and ASNs, inspects them, and puts lots away into subinventories.
functions: Receipts against POs and advance shipment notices
Inspection before delivery (food safety)
Lot numbers and expiry dates captured at receipt

nodes.title: Inventory
nodes.subtitle: On hand · lots · subinventories
nodes.description: On-hand quantities by organisation, subinventory and lot; issues, transfers, cycle counts and lot expiry.
functions: Lot control with expiry dates; first-expiry, first-out picking
Transfers between plant and distribution centre
Cycle counts and adjustments
Sends every transaction to Cost Accounting

nodes.title: Manufacturing
nodes.subtitle: Process work orders
nodes.description: Runs process work orders from the work definition: issues ingredient lots, records resources, completes finished-good lots and co-products.
functions: Process manufacturing enabled per plant
Material issue (push or backflush) by lot
Resource transactions: labour and machine hours
Product completion with lot genealogy for recall

nodes.title: Order Management
nodes.subtitle: Sales orders
nodes.description: Captures sales orders and runs an orchestration process for each fulfilment line: schedule, reserve, ship and bill.
functions: Order capture from EDI, portal or the Sales Orders for Order Hub REST API
Orchestration steps call task services: Create Inventory Reservation, Create Shipping and Wait for Shipment, Create Billing Lines and Wait for Billing
Intercompany (change of ownership) shipments start Financial Orchestration
processes: Load Interface File for Import; Import Sales Orders
Submit Financial Orchestration Events (Process Direct Sales Order Issues)

nodes.title: Shipping
nodes.subtitle: Pick · pack · ship
nodes.description: Picks lots from inventory, packs and confirms shipments; ship confirm issues inventory and triggers billing.
functions: Pick waves and pick slips
Pack and ship with carrier details
Ship Confirm issues inventory and updates the order

nodes.title: Payables
nodes.subtitle: Supplier invoices
nodes.description: Records supplier invoices, matches them to purchase orders and receipts, validates and approves them, and accounts for them.
functions: 2-way match to PO; 3-way match to receipt
Validation calculates invoice price and exchange rate variances
Approval workflow
Asset lines go to Fixed Assets as mass additions

nodes.title: Payments
nodes.subtitle: Payment runs
nodes.description: Selects due invoices, builds payments and payment files, and sends them to the bank.
functions: Payment process requests by pay group and due date
ACH and wire files per bank
Payment accounting at issue or at clearing

nodes.title: Receivables
nodes.subtitle: Invoices · receipts
nodes.description: Bills customers from fulfilled order lines, recognises revenue, and applies customer payments.
functions: AutoInvoice from fulfilled order lines
Revenue recognition
Lockbox receipts applied to invoices
Collections and credit

nodes.title: Cash Management
nodes.subtitle: Bank statements
nodes.description: Loads bank statements and reconciles them against payments, receipts and journal entries.
functions: Bank statement files transferred from the bank to the open interface
Reconciliation matching rules match statement lines to system transactions
Each bank account carries a cash and a cash clearing account
processes: Load the bank statement file (automated process)

nodes.title: Fixed Assets
nodes.subtitle: Plant equipment
nodes.description: Capitalises plant equipment from Payables invoices or receipts and depreciates it in a corporate book and tax books.
functions: Mass additions from Payables asset lines (Create Mass Additions) or from Receiving
Corporate book → primary ledger; MX tax book → MX secondary ledger (Perform Periodic Mass Copy)
Retirements and transfers between plants
No asset REST resources in the 26C Financials catalogue (only asset book and category lists of values); additions load through FA_MASS_ADDITIONS

nodes.title: Expenses
nodes.subtitle: Employee expenses
nodes.description: Employee expense reports and corporate card transactions, approved and paid through Payables.
functions: Expense reports with receipts and policy checks
Corporate card transactions
Approved reports become Payables invoices

nodes.title: Integration endpoints
nodes.subtitle: ERP Integrations · business events · B2B
nodes.description: The REST entry points external systems use to load and extract data in bulk, follow scheduled processes and react to business events.
functions: ERP Integrations runs FBDI: importBulkData uploads the zip to UCM, loads the interface tables and submits the import process; exportBulkData runs a job and returns its output
Other operations: uploadFileToUCM, submitESSJobRequest, loadAndImportData, extractAndPurge; callbacks and bell or email notifications when a load finishes
ERP Data Integrations: upload a file and get its status, transaction counts and exceptions
ERP Business Events: which business events are enabled; ERP Processes: process details
SCM B2B messages for EDI with customers and suppliers

nodes.title: Banks
nodes.subtitle: US and MX banks
nodes.description: FBCo's banks: payment files in, lockbox and statement files out.
functions: Receives payment files
Sends lockbox files and daily bank statements

nodes.title: Receipt Accounting
nodes.subtitle: Purchase accruals
nodes.description: Creates accrual accounting for receipts, matches receipt accruals to invoices, and clears the accrual account.
functions: Accrue at receipt (inventory) or at period end (expense)
Matches invoices to receipt accruals
Clears accrual balances by rule

entries.event: Expense PO accrued at period end

nodes.title: Cost Accounting
nodes.subtitle: Valuation · WIP · COGS
nodes.description: Values every inventory and work-order transaction, absorbs overhead, recognises COGS in step with revenue, and reports gross margin.
functions: Standard cost (US) and perpetual average cost (MX)
WIP valuation and variances by work order
Overhead absorption rules
COGS recognised when revenue is recognised

nodes.title: Financial Orchestration
nodes.subtitle: Intercompany trade
nodes.description: Separates the financial flow from the physical flow when FBCo México ships to FBCo US: transfer pricing and intercompany invoices.
functions: Financial orchestration flow MX plant → US distribution centre
Transfer price: cost plus a markup
Creates the intercompany AR invoice (MX) and AP invoice (US)

nodes.title: Subledger Accounting
nodes.subtitle: Create Accounting
nodes.description: Turns every subledger event into journal entries using each ledger's accounting method, and transfers them to General Ledger.
functions: Accounting methods, journal entry rule sets and account rules
Mapping sets derive accounts (for example by item category)
For Mexico writes the primary and the secondary ledger entries in one run

nodes.title: US primary ledger
nodes.subtitle: USD · corporate COA
nodes.description: FBCo US's main ledger: US GAAP, USD, the corporate chart of accounts.
functions: Receives journals from Create Accounting and Import Journals
Revaluation of MXN balances
Part of the USD ledger set

nodes.title: MX primary ledger
nodes.subtitle: MXN · corporate COA
nodes.description: FBCo México's main ledger: MXN, the corporate chart and corporate policies.
functions: Receives journals from Create Accounting and Import Journals
Copies journals to the secondary ledger and the USD reporting currency
Revaluation of USD balances

nodes.title: MX secondary ledger
nodes.subtitle: MXN · statutory COA
nodes.description: The Mexican statutory books: the local chart through the chart of accounts mapping, at subledger conversion level.
functions: Subledger level: Create Accounting writes these entries with the primary
GL journals copied at posting (journal conversion rules)
Basis for statutory and tax reporting in Mexico

nodes.title: MX reporting currency
nodes.subtitle: USD · corporate COA
nodes.description: FBCo México in USD: each posted MX primary journal is converted to USD (journal level).
functions: Same chart, calendar and method as the MX primary ledger
Converted at the daily rate when journals post
Joins the US ledger in the USD ledger set

nodes.title: Period close
nodes.subtitle: Revalue · translate · close
nodes.description: Closes the subledgers in order, then revalues, translates and closes the ledgers.
functions: Subledger close order: inventory and cost, receipt accounting, Payables, Receivables, Assets
Revaluation to unrealized gain or loss
Translation differences to the cumulative translation adjustment
Close primary, secondary and reporting ledgers

nodes.title: Intercompany & allocations
nodes.subtitle: Balancing · allocations
nodes.description: Balances journals that cross companies and allocates plant overheads and shared services.
functions: Intercompany balancing rules add due-to and due-from lines
Allocations spread overhead pools by driver

nodes.title: Reporting
nodes.subtitle: Ledger set · FRS · Smart View
nodes.description: Consolidated USD reporting across the US ledger and the MX reporting currency, plus statutory reports from the secondary ledger.
functions: Ledger set in USD across both companies
Financial Reporting and Smart View on the balances cubes
Statutory reports from the MX secondary ledger

nodes.title: Consolidation
nodes.subtitle: FCCS
nodes.description: Group consolidation: translation, eliminations and the consolidated statements.
functions: Loads trial balances from both ledgers
Eliminates intercompany balances
Consolidated financial statements

edges.label: customer, bill-to and credit → sales order

p2p.title: Procure to Pay
p2p.lede: From supplier to payment for ingredients, packaging, MRO and services. Inventory items accrue at receipt; expense items accrue at period end.

points: Supplier, sites, contacts and bank accounts
Sites assigned to the procurement and invoicing BUs

stages.title: Requisition
points: Requests from employees, or planned buy orders released by Planning Central
Hand-off: approved requisition line → PO line

stages.title: Purchase order
points: Agreements with price breaks; POs from requisitions

stages.title: Receipt
points: Receive against the PO or ASN; inspect for food safety
Lot number and expiry date captured

stages.title: Deliver to inventory
points: Put away into the ingredient subinventory
Purchase price variance against standard cost

stages.title: Invoice
points: 2-way match to PO or 3-way match to receipt

stages.title: Accrual clearing
points: Match Receipt Accruals pairs invoices with receipt accruals
Clear Receipt Accrual Balances by rule
Expense POs not yet invoiced accrue at period end

p2p.accounting_note: Account types follow Receipt Accounting, Cost Accounting and Payables in the Oracle 26C guides. Inventory purchases must accrue at receipt; expense purchases may accrue at period end.

notes.title: Two accrual policies.
notes.text: Accrue at receipt credits the accrued liability when goods arrive; accrue at period end credits Payables when the invoice is processed, and Receipt Accounting accrues uninvoiced receipts at period end.

data.title: How the ledgers relate
data.lede: FBCo US has one primary ledger. FBCo México has a primary ledger in MXN, a secondary ledger with the Mexican statutory chart, and a USD reporting currency. Select a ledger or a step to see how data reaches it.

nodes.title: Subledgers
nodes.subtitle: AP · AR · Cost · Receipt · Assets
nodes.description: Subledger transactions in both countries raise accounting events.
functions: Create Accounting applies the accounting method of each ledger
For Mexico one run creates primary and secondary journals (subledger level)

nodes.title: Asset books
nodes.subtitle: Corporate book · MX tax book
nodes.description: Fixed Assets keeps one corporate book per primary ledger. The MX tax book is assigned to the MX secondary ledger.
functions: Corporate book: Create Accounting for Assets → primary ledger
Tax book: Perform Periodic Mass Copy from the corporate book, then accounted to the secondary ledger
Payables asset invoices and the tax-book addition use the same conversion rate, so asset clearing clears in both ledgers

nodes.title: GL journals
nodes.subtitle: Manual · spreadsheet · GL_INTERFACE
nodes.description: Journals entered in GL or imported through GL_INTERFACE.
functions: Posting in the MX primary ledger copies them to the secondary ledger (journal conversion rules)
Posting also converts them to the USD reporting currency

nodes.title: US primary ledger
nodes.subtitle: USD · corporate COA · US GAAP
nodes.description: The main record of FBCo US.
functions: Corporate chart of accounts, accounting calendar, USD
Revalues MXN balances (for example intercompany payables) at month end

nodes.title: MX primary ledger
nodes.subtitle: MXN · corporate COA
nodes.description: The main record of FBCo México, kept in the local currency on the corporate chart so that group reporting is consistent.
functions: Corporate chart and corporate accounting policies
Source for the secondary ledger and the USD reporting currency
Revalues USD balances (for example supplier invoices in USD)

nodes.title: MX secondary ledger
nodes.subtitle: MXN · statutory COA
nodes.description: The Mexican statutory books, linked to the MX primary ledger.
functions: Data conversion level: Subledger
Different chart of accounts (Mexican statutory) through the chart of accounts mapping
Same currency as the primary (MXN), which avoids difficult reconciliations

nodes.title: MX reporting currency
nodes.subtitle: USD · corporate COA
nodes.description: FBCo México's primary ledger restated in USD.
functions: Currency conversion level: Journal
Shares the chart, calendar and accounting method of the MX primary ledger
Revaluation journals in the primary are converted and posted here too

nodes.title: USD ledger set
nodes.subtitle: US primary + MX reporting currency
nodes.description: Groups the two USD views so close processes and reports run once.
functions: Open and close periods, revaluation and reports for both at once
Financial Reporting and Smart View in USD

nodes.title: Translation
nodes.subtitle: Cumulative translation adjustment
nodes.description: Balance-level translation of the MX ledger, for consolidation views that need period-end and historical rates.
functions: Translate General Ledger Account Balances
Equity at historical rates; difference to the cumulative translation adjustment

nodes.title: Consolidation
nodes.subtitle: FCCS
nodes.description: Group consolidation with eliminations.
functions: Loads both companies' trial balances
Eliminates intercompany balances

edges.label: corporate book: Create Accounting for Assets
journals converted to USD as they post

notes.title: Conversion levels.
notes.text: Secondary ledger: Balance, Journal, Subledger or Adjustment Only. Reporting currency: Balance, Journal or Subledger. Oracle advises journal level when a subledger-level ledger is added while transactions are in flight.

data.title: REST APIs
data.lede: Every top-level REST resource in Oracle's Financials, SCM and Procurement REST catalogues, with the module it belongs to on this map. Child resources (lines, distributions, attachments, flexfields) are reached through their parent. Any FBDI file can also be loaded through the ERP Integrations resource.
